etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from French naïve, feminine form of naïf, from Latin nativus (“native, natural”). Doublet of native.

definitions.definition: Lacking worldly experience, wisdom, or judgement; unsophisticated.

quote.citation: 1965, Richard Rogers, Oscar Hammerstein II (lyrics and music), “Going on Seventeen”, in The Sound of Music‎[1]:
quote.text: I am sixteen going on seventeen, I know that I'm naive

quote.citation: 2008, BioWare, Mass Effect (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →ISBN, →OCLC, PC, scene: Krogan: Genophage Codex entry:
quote.text: The salarians believed the genophage would be used as a deterrent, a position the turians viewed as naive. Once the project was complete, the turians mass produced and deployed it. The krogan homeworld, their colonies, and all occupied worlds were infected.

definitions.definition: Not having been exposed to something.

quote.citation: 2011, Lila Miller, Kate Hurley, Infectious Disease Management in Animal Shelters:
quote.text: Animals entering shelters are either (a) immunologically naïve and susceptible to infection and development of disease if exposed to pathogens; (b) already immune  […]

definitions.definition: (of art) Produced in a simple, childlike style, deliberately rejecting sophisticated techniques.

quote.text: By 1921 when Miró painted his key work, naive painting had been recognized by the avantgarde art world as a genre in its own right.

definitions.definition: (computing) Intuitive; designed to follow the way ordinary people approach a problem.

quote.citation: 2007, Takao Terano, Huan Liu, Arbee L.P. Chen, Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, →ISBN:
quote.text: We have experiments of running our matching algorithm and a naive matching algorithm for such a term tree and a tree, and have compared the performance of the two algorithms.

quote.citation: 2010, Daphne Oz, The Dorm Room Diet:
quote.text: As a seasoned woman—of nineteen—I felt it was my place to tell each of these naïves that such plans were easier made than followed.

quote.citation: 2018, King Midas, Stupid Brokers - Stupid Clients:
quote.text: In other words, they'd buy securities from these naives for 55 and sell them similar securities for 65. In plain English, they'd pay $550 per $1,000 bond and turn right around and sell them similar stuff for $650.
